symptoms: Leaves appear green and generally free of abnormal spots or lesions.
recommendations: Continue normal watering, nutrition, monitoring and good garden hygiene.
prevention: Maintain good airflow, appropriate watering and inspect plants regularly.

symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots may occur on leaves and fruit.
causes: Bacterial infection favored by wet conditions and splashing water.
recommendations: Remove severely affected foliage, avoid overhead watering and improve airflow.
prevention: Avoid working with wet plants and reduce leaf wetness.

symptoms: Brown circular lesions, often with concentric ring patterns, and yellowing around affected tissue.
causes: Fungal disease commonly associated with Alternaria species.
recommendations: Remove severely affected leaves, improve airflow, mulch soil to reduce splash and avoid overhead watering.
prevention: Rotate crops, remove infected plant debris and keep foliage dry.

symptoms: Dark irregular lesions that can expand rapidly, sometimes with pale or gray growth under humid conditions.
recommendations: Remove severely infected material and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. Seek local agricultural guidance for treatment options.
prevention: Improve airflow, avoid overhead watering and monitor plants during cool wet weather.

symptoms: Yellow patches may develop on the upper leaf surface with olive or grayish fungal growth underneath.
causes: Fungal disease favored by high humidity.
recommendations: Increase ventilation, reduce humidity and remove severely affected leaves.
prevention: Provide adequate plant spacing and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and lighter centers, frequently beginning on older leaves.
causes: Fungal disease caused by Septoria species.
recommendations: Remove heavily affected leaves, improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.
prevention: Remove plant debris and maintain good garden sanitation.

symptoms: Fine stippling, yellowing or bronzing of leaves; severe infestations may produce webbing.
recommendations: Inspect leaf undersides and use an appropriate integrated pest-management approach.
prevention: Monitor plants regularly and avoid conditions that encourage mite outbreaks.

symptoms: Brown lesions that can have concentric target-like rings.
causes: Fungal disease associated with warm, humid conditions.
recommendations: Remove severely affected leaves, improve airflow and minimize leaf wetness.
prevention: Use good sanitation and avoid prolonged moisture on foliage.

symptoms: Leaf curling, yellowing and reduced plant growth may occur.
causes: Viral disease commonly associated with whitefly transmission.
recommendations: Remove severely affected plants when appropriate and control vectors using integrated pest management.
prevention: Monitor and manage whiteflies and remove infected plant material.

symptoms: Mottled or mosaic patterns on leaves, sometimes accompanied by distorted growth.
recommendations: Remove severely affected plants and sanitize hands and gardening tools.
prevention: Use clean tools, avoid handling plants after touching infected material and use healthy planting material.
